voiceover: Your computer can't connect to a name. It needs a number, an IP address. So when you hit enter, it first checks its own memory: have I looked this up recently? If not, it asks a resolver, usually run by your internet provider or a public DNS service. The resolver asks a root server, which points it to the servers for the ending, like dot com. Those point it to the site's own name server, which finally answers: here's the IP. That's DNS, basically the internet's contacts app. The answer gets cached, so next time it's instant. Part two: now your computer has to say hi.
